chunks: As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from al-Hasan ibn ʿAli, from Ahmad ibn Hilal, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Aban ibn ʿUthman, from Zurarah, from one of the two عليهما السلام, who said:

I said: A man entered a thicket in which there is no water, but there is mud; what should he do? He said: He performs tayammum, for it is saʿid. I said: But he is riding and cannot dismount out of fear, and he is not in a state of wudu (ablution). He said: If he fears for himself from a beast or something else, and fears the passing of the time, then let him perform tayammum: he strikes with his hand upon the felt and the pack-saddle, performs tayammum, and performs salat (prayer).

So it does not contradict the report of Abi Basir and the report of Rifaʿah, for in them he said: If you are not able to reach felt or a saddle that you can shake, then perform tayammum with mud. And in this report he said: He does not perform tayammum with mud. So if he is not able to dismount due to fear, he performs tayammum from the saddle, because the proper way of reconciling the reports is that when there is dust in the felt of the saddle or the garment, it is obligatory that he perform tayammum from it and not perform tayammum from mud. Then if there is no dust in the garment in the first place, he performs tayammum with mud. But if he fears dismounting, he performs tayammum from the garment even if there is no dust in it. And that which indicates that tayammum with felt and saddle is only permissible for him when there is dust in them...

key_terms.الصَّعِيدُ: earthly ground-material qualifying as the basis for tayammum in this context
key_terms.اللِّبْدِ: felt or saddle-pad upon which the hand is struck for tayammum
key_terms.الْأَجَمَةَ: a thicket or marshy woodland entered by the person in the case described
key_terms.الْبَرْذَعَةِ: the pack-saddle or riding pad used in the tayammum scenario
key_terms.الْغُبَارُ: dust whose presence determines the validity of tayammum on saddle-felt or cloth
key_terms.سَبُعٍ: a predatory beast from which a person may fear harm
key_terms.طِينٌ: mud used in the discussion of tayammum when water is absent
key_terms.وُضُوءٍ: ritual ablution, which the rider lacks in the scenario

ai.seo_question: How should tayammum be performed when there is only mud and a person cannot dismount due to fear?
ai.summary: This report addresses the fiqh of tayammum when water is unavailable and the ground is muddy. It explains that mud may serve for tayammum, and in circumstances of fear and inability to dismount, tayammum may be done using the saddle or felt, with reconciliation given between differing reports based on the presence of dust.
